description: This course covers the fundamentals of Virtual Reality (VR) systems, including 3D modeling with Maya and Blender; VR hardware such as Oculus Rift, HTC Vive, and Microsoft HoloLens; VR software development using Unity and Unreal Engine; physics-based simulation with PhysX and Bullet; spatial audio using OpenAL and HRTF; and VR user interface design with A-Frame and WebXR. The course also explores VR networking protocols like WebRTC and VRML, as well as VR standards such as OpenXR and VRLens. Students will analyze VR rendering techniques, including ray tracing and foveated rendering, and evaluate the performance of VR applications on different platforms. The course emphasizes the practical application of VR technologies to real-world problems in fields such as gaming, education, and healthcare.

clos.text: Define the key components of a VR system, including hardware, software, and network protocols.
Describe the architecture of VR development environments such as Unity and Unreal Engine.
Explain the principles of spatial audio and its implementation using OpenAL and HRTF.
Apply VR simulation techniques such as PhysX and Bullet to create interactive virtual environments.
Evaluate the performance and usability of VR applications across different platforms and standards.

topics: VR Content Creation with Maya and Blender
